Documentation for Lightspeed Revssh


Some heads-up content before diving into lightspeed Revstbssh endpoint
Option 1 (endpoint - /revstbssh)
1.	ttls – timeout
2.	region – One of three options – NA, EU, APAC 
3.	commands – the terminal commands you want to run on the devices
4.	mac_array – the list of macs you want to run the commands on
5.	mac_file – a csv/txt file instead of list of macs that contains all the macs
6.	justification – Reasoning behind why this job needs to be ran
7.	slack – a slack channel to post the final results in (defaulted to #automated-deploy-ops if not specified)
8.	max_macs – Limit to the number of devices that would actually be ssh’ed into
9.	criteria - _NW_ defaulted but it specifies what do you wanna capture as part of end results
10.	cronjob – you can specify a cron syntax for the ssh job to run periodically (e.g. 0 9 * * *)
11.	time_zone only when using cron to specify which time zone does this cron need to follow. Currently only supports US (east )
Additionally with the above options
Option 2 (endpoint - /shell_file)
1.	upload_file – a file you want to upload to devices (for eg a binary that install an app)
2.	shell_file_params – the uploaded shell file can be ran with additional parameters during runtime
3.	upload_file_copy_location – the location the shell file will be uploaded onto in the device
4.	save_file_location – download a file/folder from the device onto sharepoint
Dynamic flows
Additional option uses ELK to dynamicall pull devices using a query
1.	mac_count – number of macs to pull from ELK
2.	user_query – ELK query to pull devices with a specific marker
3.	loopback- lookback time for the query to pull devices within the last x mins (e.g. last 1 hr)
4.	profile – one of three options RDKB, RDKV, RDKC
5.	host – one of two options on ELK – Telemetry or XDP
6.	interval_control – interval of retries on devices until success (e.g. 2 – retries every 2 mins until success)






Revssh Option 1 – Run commands  


ep = "https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/revstbssh"

def send_lightspeed_request(ep, method, token, headers=None, payload=None):
    headers = headers or {}
    headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
    # headers["Content-Type"] = "multipart/form-data"
    headers["Accept"] = "application/json"


    response = requests.request(method, ep, headers=headers, data=payload,timeout=60)

    if response.status_code >= 400:
        raise Exception(f"{response.status_code}: {response.text}")

    return response

form1 = {
            "ttls": "20",
            "region": "NA",
            "commands": "systemctl status service",
            "mac_array": mac_list_1,
	#"mac_file": 
            "justification": "CPERM-XXXXX Check service status
            #"slack": "lightspeed-testing",
            "max_macs": 10,
            "criteria": "_NW_"
        }

send_lightspeed_request(ep, "POST", access_token_ssh, payload=form1)

This request spits out a trace ID than can be used to access the results.

1.	Additionally sending a mac_file instead of a mac_list

files = {
    'mac_array': (None, ''),
    'ttls': (None,'20'),
    'region': (None,'NA'),
    'commands': (None,"systemctl status service"),
    'mac_file': ('input.csv', open('input123.csv', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'slack': (None, lightspeed-testing),
    'cronjob': (None, ''),
    'time_zone': (None, ''),
    'justification': (None, 'test'),
    'max_macs': (None, ''),
    "criteria": (None, "_NW_")
}

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/revstbssh', headers=headers, files=files)


Revssh Option 2 – Run commands from a shell script


files = {
    'mac_array': (None, ''),
    'ttls': (None,'20'),
    'region': (None,'NA'),
    'shell_file': ('fix.sh',open('fix.sh', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'shell_file_params': (None, 'Testing'),
    'mac_file': ('input.csv', open('input123.csv', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'slack': (None, 'gears-test-rahul'),
    'cronjob': (None, ''),
    'time_zone': (None, ''),
    'justification': (None, 'test'),
    'max_macs': (None, ''),
    "criteria": (None, "_NW_")
}

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/shell_file, headers=headers, files=files)

additionally you can give command line arguments to the shell file you want to run commands through 'shell_file_params'

This request spits out a trace ID than can be used to access the results.

Revssh Option 3 - SCP to Device


files = {
    'mac_array': (None, ''),
    'ttls': (None,'20'),
    'region': (None,'NA'),
    'shell_file': ('fix.sh',open('fix.sh', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'upload_file': ('testy',open('testy', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'shell_file_params': (None, 'Testing'),
    'mac_file': ('input.csv', open('input123.csv', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'upload_file_copy_location': (None, '/media'),
    'slack': (None, 'Lightspeed-testing'),
    'cronjob': (None, ''),
    'time_zone': (None, ''),
    'justification': (None, 'test'),
    'max_macs': (None, ''),
    "criteria": (None, "_NW_")
}

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/shell_file', headers=headers, files=files)
print(response.status_code, response.text)

Additionally, you can send command line arguments to the shell file you want to run commands through 'shell_file_params' with the location of the file on the device it needs to be uploaded to ‘upload_file_copy_location'.

This request spits out a trace ID than can be used to access the results.


Revssh Option 3 - SCP from Device


files = {
    'mac_array': (None, ''),
    'ttls': (None,'20'),
    'region': (None,'NA'),
    'mac_file': ('input.csv', open('input123.csv', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'slack': (None, 'gears-test-rahul'),
    'save_file_location': (None, '/tmp/top.txt'),
    'justification': (None, 'test'),
    'max_macs': (None, ''),
    "criteria": (None, "_NW_")
}

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/scpFrom, headers=headers, files=files)
print(response.status_code, response.text)

Revssh Dynamic 
All the above options come with a choice of dynamic where instead of a static mac list you could use an ELK query to pull devices on the go

files = {
    'user_query': (None, 'device.model: *'),
    'loopback': (None,'2h'),
    'region': (None,'NA'),
    'shell_file': ('fix.sh',open('fix.sh', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'upload_file': ('testy',open('testy', 'rb'), 'text/csv'),
    'shell_file_params': (None, 'Testing'),
    'profile': (None, 'RDKB'),
    'host': (None, 'TELEMETRY'),
    'slack': (None, 'gears-test-rahul'),
    'cronjob': (None, '0 9 * * *'),
    'time_zone': (None, 'US/Eastern'),
    'justification': (None, 'test'),
    'max_macs': (None, ''),
    "criteria": (None, "_NW_")
}

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/revstbsshDynamic', headers=headers, files=files)
print(response.status_code, response.text)’

OR

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/shell_file_dynamic', headers=headers, files=files)
print(response.status_code, response.text)


OR

response = requests.post('https://axiom-lightspeed.rdkops.comcast.net/scpFromDynamic, headers=headers, files=files)
print(response.status_code, response.text)
